stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the cannon barrel to aim, use the $v_0$ slider to set launch speed, then press FIRE. Try at least two different angles and change $v_0$ to see how the trajectory reacts.
stages.concept: Parabolic trajectory: $x = v_0 \cos\alpha \cdot t$, $z = v_0 \sin\alpha \cdot t - \tfrac{1}{2} g t^2$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit all three targets. The dashed preview arc shows where the projectile will land — aim, adjust, then fire.
stages.concept: Range: $x_P = \dfrac{v_0^{2} \sin(2\alpha)}{g}$ — maximum at $\alpha = 45^{\circ}$. Complementary angles give the same range.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview arc. Read each target's coordinates $(x, z)$ and pick $\alpha$ and $v_0$ so the projectile clears the wall AND lands on the target. Peek reveals the arc briefly if you need to verify.
stages.concept: Peak height: $z_S = \dfrac{v_0^{2} \sin^{2}\alpha}{2g}$. To clear an obstacle at height $h$, ensure $z(x_{\text{obstacle}}) > h$.

labels.tip2: use the preview arc to line up each target
labels.tip3: compute α and v₀ from the target coordinates, then FIRE

1.1: Drag the barrel up or down to change the launch angle α.
1.2: The v₀ slider on the right controls initial speed. Higher v₀ = further reach.
1.3: Watch how the parabola stretches with v₀ and how its shape changes with α.

2.1: The dashed arc previews the projectile's path. Line it up with a target before firing.
2.2: Higher targets need a steeper α. Distant targets need more v₀ or an α closer to 45°.
2.3: Two different α values (complementary: α₁ + α₂ = 90°) reach the same ground point — try both.

3.1: Read each target's (x, z) coordinates. Choose α, v₀ so the parabola passes through them.
3.2: Range: x_P = v₀²·sin(2α)/g. Height at x: z(x) = x·tan α − g·x² / (2·v₀²·cos²α).
3.3: For the wall: pick α, v₀ such that z(x_wall) > h_wall. Peek to verify your arc before firing.
